title: Mapo Tofu
subtitle: Sichuan spiced tofu with pork in a fiery sauce
excerpt: Mapo tofu is one of Sichuan's most celebrated dishes. Silken tofu sits in a deeply spiced sauce of doubanjiang chilli bean paste, ground pork, and stock. The result is intensely savoury, mouth-numbing, and warming. It cooks in under 30 minutes and is a benchmark of Chinese home cooking.
sourceNotes: Mapo tofu is a Sichuan dish named after a pockmarked (ma) old woman (po) who supposedly invented it in Chengdu in the Qing dynasty. The dish combines silken tofu with ground pork in a deeply spiced, numbing sauce of doubanjiang chilli bean paste and Sichuan peppercorns. It is one of the most celebrated dishes in Chinese cuisine.

content.text: Mapo tofu moves quickly once the pan is hot. The doubanjiang paste does most of the flavour work. Handle the tofu gently -- fold rather than stir -- and it will stay in clean cubes rather than crumbling. Have the cornflour slurry ready to go before you start.

items.prepNote: use 400g firm silken tofu -- cut into 2cm cubes
use 2 tbsp doubanjiang chilli bean paste
mix with 2 tbsp cold water -- for thickening
use soy sauce -- add at the end for seasoning

content.text: Heat the oil in a wok or wide pan over high heat. Add the pork mince and stir-fry until browned and starting to crisp -- about 4 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger, and doubanjiang paste. Stir-fry for 1 minute. The paste will turn the oil red.
Add the chilli flakes and stock. Bring to a simmer.
Gently slide in the tofu cubes. Do not stir vigorously or they will break. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir the cornflour mix and pour it in. Gently fold through until the sauce thickens. Season with soy sauce.
Scatter spring onion over the top. Serve immediately with steamed rice.

items.cause: Tofu too soft or stirred too vigorously
items.fix: Use firm silken tofu rather than soft silken. Slide it in gently and use a spoon to turn the whole dish rather than stirring. The tofu heats through without needing to be moved much.

content.text: Mapo tofu is one of China's most famous dishes. The combination of mouth-numbing Sichuan pepper, chilli heat, and soft tofu is unlike anything else. The dish comes from Chengdu, the capital of Sichuan province. It is quick to make and intense in flavour.
